description:
We will begin our photo session at the Louvre Pyramid, we'll walk from there to Eiffel Tower through Seine riverside taking photos along the way (Louvre Pyramid, Arc de triomphe du Carrousel, Jardin des Tuileries, Alexandre III bridge, Seine river banks, Eiffel Tower seen from Trocadéro area, stairs with Eiffel Tower view).

The walking distance from Louvre Pyramid to the Eiffel Tower is 50 minutes, so you'll need very comfortable shoes.

Recommended for:
- couples
- solo travelers
- families
- groups of friends

This experience is a private sunrise photo session during which we will be exploring some of the most beautiful places in Paris.

Other things to note
The price is per person.
This experience is a private tour.

If you have special wishes up front be sure to contact me.
hostdescription:
My name is Tatiana and I love telling stories through photography. I am a photographer based in Paris. I've been taking photos for the past 5 years (portrait photography, wildlife photography, event photography).

I invite you to make amazing photo memories and capture the emotions and beauty of your Paris vacation.
locationDescription: Louvre Pyramid and the courtyard of the Louvre Museum (Cour Napoléon) the Seine river banks Pont Alexandre-III Eiffel Tower

I received over 100 amazing pictures from Tatiana in the 1.5 hours that we spent together so I am really happy with the product. I really love walking so the photo shoot walk was amazing with awesome views of the Eiffel Tower. The walk was almost an hour long so make sure you are wearing comfy shoes. I wore my cute and comfy platform combat boots.

There are a bunch of great locations that we stopped by to grab a few shots, so you do need to have an idea of how you are posing as there is very little to no direction on “modeling” - just low key whatever feels natural to you. The stops were also a quick 1-2 minute shoot so there is very little time to change if you planned on doing so. I wanted to take off my sweater at some points but didn’t want it on the wet ground. The other thing is that if you do bring a bag, you do end up leaving it on the ground or bench somewhere and need to keep an eye on it during the photo shoot. I did mine early so it wasn’t crowded but I can only imagine my anxiety level if it were during a much crowded setting so best to leave the bag or maybe use it as an accessory for the photos.

Overall, if you are down to speed walk 2.3 miles (3.7km) with quick photo shoot shots as your rest, then this is for you, as you get a great variety of shots. If not, you may want to discuss with Tatiana if you want to focus more on the Lourve end or the Eiffel Tower end if possible. :)
